# The manifest holds the two fields that differ between two runs over one tree, and the committed export
# replaces both. This line pins what a corpus with no repository behind it writes in one of them.
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "commit": null

# The manifest says what this export is, and what it could not resolve.
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "formatVersion": 2
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "target": "none"
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "humanTemplate": null
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "rawTemplate": null
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "type": "glossary"

# Two counts, named apart: three records, five terms between them. One number would be read as either,
# and the term count is not derivable without opening the flat file.
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "records": 3
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "parts": 5
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "partsFile": "glossary/terms.jsonl"

# A record carries what `export:` in the schema declares, and not what it does not. `owner` stays
# behind: it is a fact about this corpus's stewardship rather than about the words.
.dist/export/glossary/gls-search.json :: "narrows": "gls-estate"
.dist/export/glossary/gls-search.json :: "status": "draft"
.dist/export/glossary/gls-search.json :: "review-by": "2030-01-01"
.dist/export/glossary/gls-search.json :: !"owner"

# One spelling of absent, in every file and for every key. A root narrows nothing, and says so the way
# a term with no labelled line says it.
.dist/export/glossary/gls-estate.json :: "narrows": null
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "not":null

# Prose arrives unwrapped: the corpus's 120-column wrap is a fact about the file, and a grep for a
# phrase straddling it would match nothing. The blank line the author wrote is kept.
.dist/export/glossary/gls-estate.json :: "Scope": "What every system here has in common: the words a reader meets whichever system they arrived from, and the ones a newcomer has to be told.\n\nA word one system uses its own way
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "not":"a branch in source control. Both appear in the same sentence often enough to be worth separating, and a reader arriving from either one will read the other as a mistake."

# A corpus with no resolvable address writes its records without links rather than with empty ones.
.dist/export/glossary/gls-search.json :: "links": null

# One term, one line, one whole object — carrying the definition and the labelled line apart, the state
# of the glossary it came from, and the record it belongs to, because a grep hands back a line and
# nothing around it. The address is the exception: a line carries the `path` and `anchor` that go into
# the manifest's templates, and no URL, so one host and one commit are stated once for the whole export.
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: {"id":"gls-search.query","title":"Query","definition":"What a reader typed, after parsing and before matching.","not":"the request the service received. One request carries a query and its paging.","seeAlso":null,"type":"glossary","record":"gls-search","part":"query","status":"draft","reviewBy":"2030-01-01","path":"glossary/search.md","anchor":"query"}
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: !"links"

# A cross-reference travels as a part id the consumer can look up, read from the anchor the link names.
# The prose keeps the reference its author wrote.
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "seeAlso":["gls-framework.record"]
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "not":"a knowledge document filed under a type — see [gls-framework.record]."

# The other half of the pair names the file and no term inside it, so there is nothing to read and
# nothing is carried. Guessing the counterpart from the term's own spelling would be right here and
# silently wrong for a pair that does not share a word.
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "record":"gls-framework","part":"record","status":"draft"
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: The catalogue uses the word for something else again — see [gls-estate].","seeAlso":null

# Generality holds inside a chain: `gls-search` narrows `gls-estate`, so a grep for a term both define
# would meet the general one first. Across `gls-estate` and `gls-framework` — unrelated roots, both
# defining `record` — the order is stable and claims nothing, so nothing here asserts it does.
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "record":"gls-estate","part":"record"
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: "record":"gls-framework","part":"record"

# A clause line and a term line share no key beyond the ones every line carries. Each type declares its
# own, so a policy's `level` and a glossary's `definition` stay in their own files.
.dist/export/policies/clauses.jsonl :: "level":"MUST"
.dist/export/policies/clauses.jsonl :: !"definition"
.dist/export/glossary/terms.jsonl :: !"level"

# A table row is not an address a renderer emits, so the two halves of a clause's address differ: `part`
# names the clause and `anchor` names the section holding the table. A term line carries them equal.
.dist/export/policies/clauses.jsonl :: "part":"TIMEBOX","status":"draft","reviewBy":"2030-01-01","path":"policies/rtnt-retention.md","anchor":"clauses"

# An advisory clause carries its level like any other, so a consumer filtering on obligation drops it
# without reading the words.
.dist/export/policies/clauses.jsonl :: "level":"SHOULD"

# One manifest entry per exporting type, each carrying its own shape version and its own fidelities.
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "type": "policies"
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "partsFile": "policies/clauses.jsonl"
.dist/export/manifest.json :: "Purpose": "summary"

# The definitions sit in a block at the foot of the record, which is inside whichever section is written
# last. They render as nothing, so the section a consumer reads as prose ends on the author's words.
.dist/export/policies/pol-RTNT.json :: "Exceptions": "A store under a legal hold outlives its retention period. We record the hold against the store, and the period resumes on the day the hold lifts."
.dist/export/policies/pol-RTNT.json :: !gls-estate

# A clause's cross-reference has no body to be read from, so the id it names stays inside the words.
.dist/export/policies/clauses.jsonl :: "clause":"MUST record a legal hold against whatever gls-estate calls a store"
.dist/export/policies/clauses.jsonl :: !"seeAlso"
